subject: ShieldWave: IR notification and evidence handoff request
messages:
From: Jared Cole <jared.cole@shieldwave.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: security-oncall@shieldwave.com
Date: Sun, 01 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Possible data-exfil pattern observed — need IR plan + evidence

Hi Mateo / Marissa,

We observed an unusual outbound traffic pattern from one of our integration endpoints that overlaps with Redwood-hosted inference calls (see attached screenshot). We don't believe customer data was exfiltrated, but per our compliance team we need to treat this as a security event and collect the following from Redwood for our SOC 2 / SIG evidence: 

- Time-windowed access logs (S3, inference API) for 2026-11-01 01:00–09:00 UTC
- SIEM export (raw events) for the same window
- List of service accounts with access to the affected model + most recent IAM change events
- Any KV-cache eviction logs / anomalous sequence IDs if available
- Point of contact for evidence transfer and expected SLA for delivery (48–72h preferred)

Please advise if you'd prefer a secure S3 transfer or a signed Drive link. Also loop in your security contact for a quick sync today if possible — ShieldWave is aiming to close our internal notification loop by EOD tomorrow.

Attachment: shieldwave-suspicious-traffic-screenshot.png (PNG, 180KB)

Thanks,
Jared Cole
Director, Security Operations
ShieldWave Financial
From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
To: Jared Cole <jared.cole@shieldwave.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 01 Nov 2026 09:45:12 -08:00
Subject: Re: Possible data-exfil pattern observed — need IR plan + evidence

Thanks for the heads-up, Jared — we appreciate the clear ask and the screenshot.

Immediate plan:
- I've opened an internal incident and assigned primary owners: Marissa (forensics lead), Neha (controls / SOC 2 mapping), Rishi (network / infra).
- We'll gather the requested artifacts and surface an evidence delivery plan within 4 business hours. If we need extended access to ShieldWave systems for correlation, we'll coordinate through your security-oncall address.

Requested from you: preferred transfer method (S3 vs Drive) and confirmation of the exact SCP/endpoint IPs involved so we can filter logs precisely.

I've attached an IR_Action_Items_Template.xlsx to track artifacts and owners.

Onboarding notes for our internal team: please pull:
- API access logs (token-level) for the specified window
- Ingress/egress VPC flow logs and NAT gateway flows
- Auth audit events for service accounts created/modified in the prior 30 days
- KV-cache evictions and model-serving telemetry for unusual sequence gaps

We'll aim to provide a first-pass package (redacted where necessary) within 24–48 hours.

— Mateo Alvarez
Sr. Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com, Jared Cole <jared.cole@shieldwave.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, ellen.park@compliancepartners.io
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 11:22:03 -08:00
Subject: Re: Possible data-exfil pattern observed — need IR plan + evidence

Hi all — quick update from the forensics side.

What we have so far:
- Collected API access logs and VPC flow logs for 2026-11-01 00:45–09:15 UTC. Raw exports are packaging now.
- SIEM export (Splunk) for correlated events during the window: preliminary file being generated.
- IAM audit: pulled create/modify events for service accounts over the last 30 days; no anomalous service account creations detected.
- Model-serving telemetry: there are a few KV-cache eviction events at 02:13 UTC that we are investigating (no obvious data leakage pattern yet).

Delivery plan & links:
- For secure transfer we'll push a signed, time-limited Drive link (preferred by ShieldWave per Mateo).
- Upload ETA: within 6 hours for initial package (logs redacted for PII). Full artifacts (forensics_package_20261102.zip) to follow with checksums.

Mapping note: Neha is preparing a quick SOC 2 / SIG crosswalk that maps these artifacts to common control objectives (CC6, CC7 and SIG data protection families). That doc will help your compliance reviewers validate the evidence.

Attachment: forensics_package_20261102.zip (packaging in-progress)

— Marissa Cole
Lead Forensics Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Jared Cole <jared.cole@shieldwave.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: security-oncall@shieldwave.com
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 08:05:20 -08:00
Subject: Re: Possible data-exfil pattern observed — need IR plan + evidence

Appreciate the fast turnaround. A few follow-ups from ShieldWave compliance:

- Please include network flow logs at 1-minute granularity if available (we need fine-grain correlation for our audit).
- Can your team confirm retention configuration for the raw logs (S3 lifecycle/retention policy) and provide an attestation we can keep for our SOC 2 file?
- If possible, include a short statement on whether any customer PII was part of the tokens sent during the window — we understand you may need to redact specifics but an attestation is helpful.

We prefer the signed Drive transfer. Our team will acknowledge on receipt and escalate to our internal auditors.

Thanks,
Jared
From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
To: Jared Cole <jared.cole@shieldwave.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, ellen.park@compliancepartners.io
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 15:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Possible data-exfil pattern observed — need IR plan + evidence (closure)

Jared / ShieldWave team — final update and postmortem summary attached. Highlights: 

- Findings: No confirmed exfiltration of customer data. Traffic spike caused by an upstream partner retry storm combined with an edge NAT misconfiguration that amplified outbound flows. Root cause is external -> remediation: partner throttle + Redwood NAT egress rule tightened.
- Artifacts delivered: forensics_package_20261102.zip (S3+VPC logs), soc2-sig-caiq-crosswalk-20261103.pdf, and postmortem_shieldwave_20261104.pdf (contains timeline, action owners, and verification checklist). Drive link shared (see related_links).
- Retention & attestation: Raw logs are retained per our standard 90-day S3 lifecycle for hot logs; forensic exports generated for this event will be retained for 1 year under our incident evidence retention policy. Attached is a short attestation statement for ShieldWave auditors.
- PII statement: We confirm no customer PII was observed in the payloads within the inspected window. We have redacted any non-essential identifiers from the packaged artifacts.

Next steps: schedule a 45-minute tabletop in two weeks to review the incident and controls update; Neha will coordinate a SOC 2 evidence refresh for any controls affected.

Attachment: postmortem_shieldwave_20261104.pdf; soc2-sig-caiq-crosswalk-20261103.pdf

If you'd like an export in another format or additional log granularity for your auditors, let us know and we'll extend the package.

— Mateo Alvarez
Sr. Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
